docs.text:
Prepare bounded edits of full cylindrical through-holes in one solid.

Accepts a B-Rep returned by read_step; does not assume a stock primitive or a construction history. Each selected inward cylinder must be complete, with two perpendicular planar ends and sufficient clearance. Blind, split, oblique, intersecting and near-boundary holes are unsupported. Rejected inward cylinders are reported; an explicit selection of one raises.

frame maps input units to working coordinates; by default the bounding box is centered and its largest extent becomes 40 working units. It is frozen during editing. deflection is an absolute WORKING-unit meshing tolerance, finite and positive. Preparation requires JAX x64; it never changes the global JAX precision setting. Input CAD is copied.

Radius bounds are [0.5r0, r0 + 0.2clearance]. Optional transverse center shifts share the growth budget: norm(shift) + max(radius-r0, 0) must not exceed 0.2*clearance. Moving cylinder samples and neighboring planar samples together preserves the welded connectivity. Geometry outside the radial support stays fixed. These are local edits, not a topology-changing CAD kernel. Mesh orientation may restrict the usable interval further; callers must check model.is_valid.

Raises ValueError for invalid CAD, unsupported selections, no supported holes, or a mesh that cannot be welded into a closed oriented surface. Unsupported surface evaluators raise NotImplementedError. OCCT extraction failures propagate. Meshing accuracy is not certified by preparation.

Example

import jax from brepax.io.step import read_step jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) edit = prepare_hole_edit(read_step("plate_with_holes.step")) radii = (edit.model.reference_radii + edit.model.upper_radii) / 2 assert bool(edit.model.is_valid(radii)) volume, gradient = jax.jit(jax.value_and_grad(edit.model.volume))(radii) edited_cad = edit.rebuild(radii)

To move a hole, pass center_shifts in external units to the model and rebuild. For a selected Z-axis hole, jnp.array([[0.1, 0.0, 0.0]]) moves its center in X; check the combined budget with is_valid first.

docs.title: Circular cut crossing a plate edge
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.contact evaluates the remaining volume of a rectangular plate after a perpendicular circular through-cut, including the transition from an enclosed hole to an open notch. It integrates the analytic boundary and differentiates that same continuous volume. It does not accept arbitrary STEP input or rebuild a solid; the imported-hole API above retains its clearance constraints.

Use a source checkout containing this experimental module for the example and benchmark below.

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

from brepax.experimental.contact import plate_with_hole_volume

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
center = jnp.array([1.5, 0.2])
half_extents = jnp.array([3.0, 2.0])
height = jnp.array(2.0)

def volume(radius):
    return plate_with_hole_volume(center, radius, half_extents, height)

# First contact is at radius 1.5; 1.7 opens the right edge.
value, derivative = jax.jit(jax.value_and_grad(volume))(jnp.array(1.7))

Use one length unit and local plate coordinates. All parameters support first derivatives; exact contact can have a smooth volume even when the solid's boundary pinches and its mesh is not closed. Moving a fully enclosed hole's center at fixed radius correctly has zero volume derivative. See ADR-0022 for the scope, numerical limitations, and comparison requirements.

Run the independent geometry and estimator comparison from a checkout:

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.contact_transition.run --cad --output /tmp/contact.json

The output retains failed cases, all declared smoothing choices, finite-difference steps, fresh OCCT and mesh checks, and synchronized execution costs. Ordinary AD of the same analytic primal is included. These bounded comparisons do not establish a general advantage over ordinary AD or arbitrary CAD support.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.contact
docs.text:
Analytic area and first shape derivatives for a circular cut in a rectangle.

This limited experiment uses Green's theorem and boundary flux, not a sampled indicator or a correction to a future contact event. It does not edit a B-Rep.

docs.title: circle_rectangle_intersection_area(center, radius, half_extents)
docs.text:
Area of a disk intersected with a centered, axis-aligned rectangle.

All inputs use one length unit. center is in the rectangle's local frame; radius and both half_extents must be positive and finite. Invalid numerical inputs return NaN for the value and first derivatives. Use floating JAX arrays of matching dtype; x64 is recommended near contact.

Supports jit, vmap, JVP and reverse-mode first derivatives in all arguments, including at circle/edge and circle/corner contacts (C1). The custom JVP integrates normal boundary velocity for the same continuous area as the primal. It avoids differentiating singular arc endpoints whose contributions cancel and arbitrary AD conventions at tied sorted endpoints. Only first derivatives are part of this contract; second derivatives may not exist at contact.

Scaling all lengths by s>0 scales area by s**2 and length derivatives by s. The local frame must move with the rectangle under rigid transformations. Tiny remaining areas and extreme radius/rectangle ratios can lose relative floating-point accuracy; this is not a general robust Boolean kernel.

Example::

area = circle_rectangle_intersection_area(
    jnp.array([1.5, 0.2]), jnp.array(1.8), jnp.array([3.0, 2.0])
)

docs.title: plate_with_hole_volume(center, radius, half_extents, height)
docs.text:
Remaining volume after a perpendicular circular through-cut in a plate.

The stock is [-bx,bx] x [-by,by] x [0,height]; the cutter spans its full height. The cut may open through edges or corners, unlike bounded fixed-topology hole editing. This function evaluates a scalar; it does not regenerate CAD or accept arbitrary STEP geometry.

Inputs are floating JAX arrays in one length unit. Positive finite sizes are required; invalid inputs produce NaN values and first derivatives. First differentiation in all arguments and JAX transformations follow circle_rectangle_intersection_area. Volume scales as length cubed and length derivatives as length squared. Interior center motion correctly has zero volume derivative. Near total stock removal, subtraction limits relative accuracy of the remaining volume.

Example::

radius = jnp.array(1.8)
objective = lambda r: plate_with_hole_volume(
    jnp.array([1.5, 0.2]), r, jnp.array([3.0, 2.0]), jnp.array(2.0)
)
volume, dvolume_dr = jax.value_and_grad(objective)(radius)

docs.title: Opposing planar face contact
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.planar_contact evaluates how intersection volume starts changing when two solids move from a known opposing planar contact. It takes a convex contact polygon and a translation/rotation direction. Unlike the circular-cut example, this is a one-sided directional response, generally nonlinear in direction, with no single gradient representing every motion.

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

from brepax.experimental.planar_contact import (
    planar_contact_volume_direction,
    prepare_planar_contact_patch,
)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
patch = prepare_planar_contact_patch(
    [[-1, -1], [1, -1], [1, 1], [-1, 1]],
    origin=[0, 0, 0], basis=[[1, 0], [0, 1], [0, 0]],
)
tilts = jnp.array([[1.0, 0, 0], [-1.0, 0, 0]])
response = jax.jit(jax.vmap(
    lambda omega: planar_contact_volume_direction(
        patch, jnp.zeros(3), omega, jnp.zeros(3)
    )
))(tilts)
# Both tilts create overlap: response == [1, 1].

The plane normal is the cross product of the basis columns, outward from the fixed solid. Inputs use one length unit; translation is length per unit of the dimensionless path parameter and rotation is radians per unit parameter. Transform both velocities and the pivot with the geometry under proper rigid motion. Scaling lengths and translation by s scales the response by s**3. Changing the pivot requires the compensating translation documented by the API. Preparation is host-only and requires x64; queries support jit and vmap with a fixed polygon size. Differentiating a response query does not produce the gradient of Boolean volume at contact.

For actual CAD inputs, prepare_planar_contact_reference in brepax.experimental.planar_contact_cad takes two solids and explicit face IDs. It checks finite convex polyhedra with straight-edged, single-wire planar faces and unique opposing supports. Its required mode distinguishes "zero_residual" from "projected_nominal". Both return a nominal support polygon, with the source gaps, normal residuals, and tolerances retained in prepared.diagnostics; neither certifies exact source contact nor repairs the solids. Even a positive gap below OCCT tolerance changes the derivative. Curved or holed faces, initial overlap, additional contact patches, and general nonconvex CAD are outside this selected-face preparation contract. The collection API below handles the separate case of explicitly supplied convex cells.

Run the grouped estimator comparison and fresh CAD direction-selection example:

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.face_contact.run --output /tmp/face-contact.json

The same finite motion candidates and action step are evaluated with actual CAD volumes. Results include calibration choices, five geometry-group splits, ablations, setup/runtime costs, and unsupported or unresolved cases. A good infinitesimal direction does not certify a finite edit; tiny CAD wedges can fall below OCCT resolution. This experiment does not add a generic optimizer, contact detector, or arbitrary STEP topology-editing API. See ADR-0022 for the decision and the directional derivation.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.planar_contact
docs.text:
One-sided volume responses from supplied opposing planar contact patches.

This is a nonlinear function of a supplied rigid-motion direction, not a custom JVP of Boolean volume or a detector of contact in arbitrary geometry.

docs.title: PlanarContactPatch
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Convex contact polygon in an oriented orthonormal plane frame.

Create with :func:prepare_planar_contact_patch outside JAX tracing. vertices are counterclockwise local coordinates without a repeated closing vertex. origin + basis @ vertex gives a world point; the cross product of the basis columns points outward from the fixed solid toward the moving solid. Geometry uses a single length unit.

The record contains no solids and cannot certify contact or isolation. Keep it fixed when querying motions. Polygon size is static under JIT; vmap over directions does not require padding or changing this size.

docs.title: PlanarContactSet
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Packed contact triangles with a fixed capacity and padding mask.

Create with :func:prepare_planar_contact_set outside JAX tracing. Each active row stores one triangle in a patch's local plane coordinates, together with that plane's origin and oriented orthonormal basis. Keeping local coordinates avoids constructing large world-space triangle vertices. The leading dimension is static under JIT; inactive rows contribute zero.

This record carries supplied geometry, not proof that its patches form a complete, nonoverlapping physical contact set. Keep it fixed when querying motion directions. Its arrays are not a differentiable CAD construction.

docs.title: prepare_planar_contact_patch(vertices, *, origin, basis)
docs.text:
Validate a convex local polygon and its world frame on the host.

Requires JAX x64. Raises ValueError for nonfinite/malformed inputs, repeated edges, nonpositive area, nonconvexity, or a nonorthonormal frame. Polygon half-plane checks reject negative orientations, including those within roundoff: accepting an uncertain negative sign can admit a thin self-crossing polygon. This conservative check may reject nearly collinear input after a coordinate transform. Frame checks use 64 float64 epsilons as a dimensionless roundoff allowance. This checks represented geometry, not the existence of a physical contact. No vertex is snapped or removed. Near-degenerate or extremely large local coordinates can lose precision and should be recentered by the caller.

docs.title: planar_contact_volume_direction(patch, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, pivot)
docs.text:
Positive one-sided derivative of intersection volume at planar contact.

The initial interiors must be disjoint, with one isolated opposing contact polygon and positive solid thickness on both sides. For the moving body's path pivot + exp(t*[angular_velocity]_cross) @ (x-pivot) + t*linear_velocity, this returns the integral of max(-normal dot (linear_velocity + angular_velocity cross (x-pivot)), 0). It measures the limit as t decreases to zero from above. A positive gap, existing overlap, or an omitted positive-area contact changes that target.

Supports jit and vmap over supplied finite directions with a fixed patch. This map is nonlinear in direction; it is not an ordinary JVP of volume. Differentiating this function would differentiate the response model, not the underlying Boolean volume. No derivative of this response map is part of the contract. Invalid motion components return NaN.

With dimensionless t, linear velocity uses length units, angular velocity radians, and the result volume units. Proper rigid transformations must also transform the frame, pivot, and both velocities. Scaling all lengths and linear velocity by s>0 scales the result by s**3. Changing pivot to p' requires v' = v + angular_velocity cross (p'-pivot) for the same instantaneous motion direction (finite paths can differ at second order). For rigid bodies, union and fixed-minus-moving volume responses have the opposite sign. Finite edits still require an independent volume check.

Uses exact affine integration over a triangle fan in float64. Very small caps, extreme scales, or cancellation in the represented velocity field can lose relative accuracy; no arbitrary-precision guarantee is made.

Example::

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
patch = prepare_planar_contact_patch(
    [[-1, -1], [1, -1], [1, 1], [-1, 1]],
    origin=[0, 0, 0], basis=[[1, 0], [0, 1], [0, 0]],
)
# Opposite tilts both create overlap: each response is 1.
value = jax.jit(planar_contact_volume_direction)(
    patch, jnp.zeros(3), jnp.array([1.0, 0, 0]), jnp.zeros(3)
)

docs.title: prepare_planar_contact_set(patches, *, capacity=None)
docs.text:
Validate and pack supplied patches into masked triangle arrays.

Requires JAX x64 and validates each patch using :func:prepare_planar_contact_patch. capacity counts triangles, not patches. Its default is the sum of len(vertices)-2 over the patches; a larger capacity pads with inactive rows. An empty input is allowed and has zero default capacity. Raises ValueError for a negative/noninteger capacity, insufficient capacity, or an invalid patch.

Patch interiors must be disjoint as surface regions and the collection must include every positive-area contact relevant to the requested volume response. These geometric conditions are the caller's responsibility: this function neither detects overlaps nor removes duplicates. Repeating a patch counts its contribution twice. Edge-sharing partitions are valid. All patches must use one length unit and outward normals from the same fixed body toward the same moving body.

docs.title: planar_contact_set_volume_direction(contacts, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, pivot)
docs.text:
Sum positive one-sided overlap responses over supplied contact patches.

Every active triangle integrates the positive normal approach speed for the common rigid motion specified by linear_velocity, angular_velocity and pivot. For two finite polyhedral bodies with initially disjoint interiors, this is the intersection-volume derivative when the supplied patches cover all positive-area opposing contacts once and the solids have positive thickness there. Contacts may share edges. Omitted or duplicated patches invalidate the full-body interpretation. Gapped, edge-only and point-only polyhedral contacts contribute no first order volume, but can contribute to a finite edit. A zero response is not a collision-free certificate; independently check every finite edit.

Supports jit and vmap over directions and equally padded sets. Empty sets return zero for finite motions. Nonfinite motion or pivot components return NaN, including for an empty set. Uses the same stable affine triangle integration as :func:planar_contact_volume_direction, with the same floating-point limits. Accumulation over many triangles can introduce additional summation error.

Units, rigid covariance, cubic length scaling and compensated-pivot laws match :func:planar_contact_volume_direction. This is a nonlinear map of the supplied direction, not an ordinary JVP. No derivative of this map or of the packed geometry is part of the contract.

Example::

unit_square = [[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1]]
floor = prepare_planar_contact_patch(
    unit_square, origin=[0, 0, 0], basis=[[1, 0], [0, 1], [0, 0]]
)
wall = prepare_planar_contact_patch(
    unit_square, origin=[0, 0, 0], basis=[[0, 0], [1, 0], [0, 1]]
)
contacts = prepare_planar_contact_set((floor, wall), capacity=8)
# Into both walls: each unit-area patch contributes one.
response = planar_contact_set_volume_direction(
    contacts, jnp.array([-1.0, 0, -1]), jnp.zeros(3), jnp.zeros(3)
)  # 2.0

docs.title: brepax.experimental.planar_contact_cad
docs.text:
Host preparation of a nominal contact patch from selected planar CAD faces.

This module prepares a planar contact model, not an exact-contact certificate or a repaired B-Rep. Source gaps and numerical residuals remain visible.

docs.title: PreparedPlanarContact dataclass
docs.text: Numerical reference patch and host-only source diagnostics.

docs.title: PlanarContactDiagnostics dataclass
docs.text:
Source-CAD evidence, in input length units unless dimensionless.

plane_distance_range contains signed moving-vertex distances from the fixed plane, whose outward normal points towards the moving solid. signed_plane_gap uses the underlying plane origins. With imperfect opposition there is no single gap, so both quantities are retained. Normal residual is dimensionless. Bounds concern floating-point geometric consistency and never replace a nonzero gap by exact source contact.

docs.title: prepare_planar_contact_reference(fixed_shape, moving_shape, *, fixed_face_id, moving_face_id, mode)
docs.text:
Prepare explicitly selected convex support polygons on the fixed plane.

Both inputs must be valid finite convex polyhedral solids with planar, convex, single-wire faces and straight edges. Face IDs index the current TopExp_Explorer(shape, TopAbs_FACE) order; rebuilding CAD can change IDs. The selected faces must oppose, be the unique faces on their support planes, and have positive-area overlap after projection. Whole-solid checks exclude competing contacts outside this convex supporting model.

mode is required. "zero_residual" rejects every computed nonzero plane or normal-opposition residual. "projected_nominal" permits only roundoff-sized residuals and explicitly projects the moving support polygon onto the fixed plane. Both return the projected support-polygon reference, not a repaired solid or a certified derivative of the original CAD. Even a positive source gap below either OCCT tolerance or roundoff has a different contact derivative; inspect the returned diagnostics and establish actual contact independently before applying the reference law to source CAD.

Lengths retain input units; linear velocities and pivots passed to the evaluator must use these units. Preparation requires JAX x64 and runs on the host. The resulting patch supports the numerical evaluator's JAX transformations. Rigid placement and positive unit scaling preserve the reference geometry up to extraction roundoff. Extreme origin/feature conditioning can fail the consistency checks instead of being snapped.

Raises ValueError for unsupported geometry, selection, residuals, or mode. No contact search, face healing, or original-solid modification occurs.

Example, given two known contacting boxes and their selected face IDs::

prepared = prepare_planar_contact_reference(
    fixed, moving, fixed_face_id=5, moving_face_id=4,
    mode="zero_residual",
)
rate = planar_contact_volume_direction(
    prepared.patch, velocity, angular_velocity, pivot,
)

docs.title: Multiple contacts from convex cells
docs.text:
prepare_planar_contact_set_reference accepts finite lists of convex polyhedral CAD cells for the fixed and moving bodies. The moving cells share one rigid motion. It checks every within-body and cross-body pair; same-body cell interiors must be disjoint, and initial cross-body overlap is rejected. All positive-area contacts contribute to the packed response. Positive gaps and edge/point contacts remain in the inventory even though their first-order volume response is zero. Shared patch edges are allowed; duplicate cells are not.

For example, a cube approaching the floor and wall of an L-shaped stock has two unit-area contact patches:

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

from brepax._occt.backend import BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox, gp_Pnt
from brepax.experimental.planar_contact import planar_contact_set_volume_direction
from brepax.experimental.planar_contact_collection_cad import (
    prepare_planar_contact_set_reference,
)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
fixed = [
    BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox(gp_Pnt(-1, 0, -1), 2, 1, 1).Shape(),
    BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox(gp_Pnt(-1, 0, 0), 1, 1, 1).Shape(),
]
moving = [BRepPrimAPI_MakeBox(gp_Pnt(0, 0, 0), 1, 1, 1).Shape()]
prepared = prepare_planar_contact_set_reference(
    fixed, moving, mode="zero_residual"
)
response = planar_contact_set_volume_direction(
    prepared.contact_set,
    jnp.array([-1.0, 0, -1]), jnp.zeros(3), jnp.zeros(3),
)  # 2.0; the finite overlap is 2*t - t**2 for small positive t.

Preparation requires JAX x64. The packed set supports jit and vmap, with optional triangle capacity and masks when preparing sets directly. Direct numerical preparation only packages the supplied patches; it cannot establish contact completeness or absence of duplicates.

The CAD collection uses represented vertex hulls for pair classification and retains source-plane residuals for its nominal contact polygons. Neither is a certificate for exact source-CAD contact. Unlike selected-face counterfactual projection, this collection never promotes a positive represented gap or interior overlap into touching: gaps stay separated and overlaps are rejected. "projected_nominal" only permits the bounded face-residual preparation after the represented pair is touching. Source faces must own the exact represented support vertices and resolve the same support plane and normal; an unresolved thin patch is rejected rather than replaced by another nearby face. Rotating and re-extracting adjacent cells can introduce tiny represented overlaps and cause conservative rejection. Preparing an explicit design in its working frame and then transforming the contact model is a distinct route; finite CAD must still be checked after actual placement.

The bounded cutter/socket example selects both a direction and a finite amount, then executes an actual stock-minus-cutter Boolean edit:

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.run \
  --output /tmp/multi-contact.json --step-output /tmp/cutter-edit.step

The report compares target-removal error and fixed-step material removal, including single-patch ablations, sampled estimators, actual CAD differences, and scanning the same finite candidates. It keeps preparation, compilation, query and Boolean costs separate. Common/Cut volume balance and valid shapes check the executed action; they do not imply that a requested target volume was achieved exactly. First-order selection can miss a better finite action. The demonstration STEP assigns millimetres to its generated working lengths and is read back to verify volume and validity; it does not infer input units.

The single-contact benchmark also records three CAD resolution routes: raw external construction, reconstruction from trusted dimensions in an explicit fixed CadFrame, and transformation of an already-built B-Rep. Reconstruction can resolve a small design feature without resolving uncertainty in imported source CAD. A coordinate transform also transforms stored tolerances and is not a substitute for constructing the design in suitable working units.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.planar_contact_collection_cad
docs.text:
Exhaustive contact preparation for two explicit convex-cell collections.

Cell-pair predicates use convex hulls of represented CAD vertex coordinates. The returned face patches use the selected-face nominal reference contract; neither reference certifies exact contact of the original CAD surfaces.

docs.title: PreparedPlanarContactSet dataclass
docs.text:
Complete pair inventory and projected patches for represented cells.

Completeness covers the supplied cells only. It does not establish that they form a decomposition of some separately supplied CAD object. Face projection residuals remain visible in patch_sources. Distinct patches may share edges; same-body represented interiors have been checked not to overlap. Empty and lower-dimensional inventories legitimately have zero first-order response, but still require finite-edit CAD verification.

docs.title: ContactPreparationError
docs.text:
Bases: ValueError

Rejected pair with retained evidence; no partial contact set is returned.

docs.title: prepare_planar_contact_set_reference(fixed_cells, moving_cells, *, mode)
docs.text:
Prepare all planar contacts between two explicit convex-cell bodies.

Each input cell must satisfy the selected-face preparation's finite convex polyhedral contract. Empty sequences are allowed. The caller supplies the decomposition: this function neither decomposes nonconvex STEP solids nor proves equality to another whole-body shape.

Extraction runs once per cell. Exact integer predicates classify the convex hulls of the binary64 topological vertex coordinates, testing face normals and every nonparallel edge-cross-edge axis without an angular cutoff. Same-body and cross-body interior overlap is rejected even when smaller than OCCT tolerances. Every positive represented gap remains separated, including sub-tolerance gaps. Edge and point contacts remain in the inventory with zero first-order contribution.

Required mode controls face preparation only after represented face contact is established. Each exposed topological vertex set must map uniquely to one source face; its normal and plane must resolve the exact represented support within the stated roundoff bounds. An unresolved small patch cannot fall back to some other nearby source-face pair. zero_residual requires computed-zero plane/opposition residuals. projected_nominal permits roundoff-sized face residuals using the existing projected-support-polygon reference. Unlike the explicitly selected single-patch API, this collection API never projects a represented positive gap or overlap into contact.

Neither mode certifies contact of the source CAD surfaces. Their trimmed planes may differ from the vertex hulls within extraction roundoff; face diagnostics preserve this distinction. A common CAD transform can turn a nominally touching partition into slightly overlapping represented hulls, which is conservatively rejected. Preparing known design-frame cells and transforming the numerical model is a separate operation, not an automatic fallback or proof about transformed source CAD.

Lengths and tolerances use input units. JAX x64 is required. This host-side exhaustive procedure targets small cell collections: hull construction enumerates vertex triples and has O(n**4) worst-case cost per cell. The returned packed set supports the numerical evaluator's jit/vmap contract. No finite collision-free step or Boolean result follows from a zero rate; independently verify every finite edit, including edge/point contacts.

Raises ValueError for unsupported cells, mode or precision, and ContactPreparationError with pair evidence for overlap or unresolved source-face preparation. No partial set or modified CAD is returned.

Example, for a cutter touching a floor and a side wall::

prepared = prepare_planar_contact_set_reference(
    (floor, wall), (cutter,), mode="zero_residual",
)
rate = planar_contact_set_volume_direction(
    prepared.contact_set, velocity, angular_velocity, pivot,
)
# Inspect prepared.cell_pairs and independently verify the finite Cut.

docs.title: Preserving a supplied placement
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.planar_contact_placement keeps local geometry and a common frame instead of baking a transformation into every vertex. With the local cells from the preceding example:

from brepax.experimental.planar_contact_placement import (
    placed_planar_contact_set_volume_direction,
    prepare_placed_planar_contact_set_reference,
)

placed = prepare_placed_planar_contact_set_reference(
    fixed, moving, rotation=jnp.eye(3), origin=(2, -1, 3),
    length_scale=0.001, mode="zero_residual",
)
rate = placed_planar_contact_set_volume_direction(
    placed.model, jnp.array([-0.001, 0, -0.001]),
    jnp.zeros(3), jnp.array([2.0, -1, 3]),
)  # 2e-9 in world volume units per dimensionless time.

The convention is world = origin + length_scale * rotation @ local. World velocities and pivot are pulled back to the local frame. Diagnostics in local_reference retain local units. A genuine shared proper-rigid top-level OCCT Location can instead be supplied through prepare_located_planar_contact_set_reference; different Location datum chains, reflections and scaled source Locations are rejected. Nested source geometry is preserved. Explicit numerical length scaling remains available separately.

This preserves supplied provenance; it cannot reconstruct a lost frame from flattened STEP vertices. Positive local gaps remain gaps and initial overlap is rejected. original_cad_contact_certified remains false. The response supports jit and vmap over motion directions, not differentiation of the prepared geometry or frame. Finite edits still require actual CAD validation.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.planar_contact_placement
docs.text:
Preserve supplied local contact geometry under a common world placement.

A placed model refers to the supplied local geometry and its explicit frame. It does not repair, reclassify, or certify a separately flattened world B-Rep.

docs.title: PlacedPlanarContactSet
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Fixed local contact model with world = origin + scale * R @ local.

Create with :func:place_planar_contact_set. rotation is proper and length_scale gives world length units per local length unit. The model keeps local support coordinates instead of rounding every CAD vertex into world coordinates. Geometry and placement stay fixed during motion queries; differentiating either record is outside the contract.

docs.title: PreparedPlacedPlanarContactSet dataclass
docs.text:
Placed numerical model and the unmodified local preparation evidence.

All dimensional pair/source diagnostics in local_reference retain local units. provenance distinguishes explicitly supplied local cells from cells whose common top-level CAD Location was retained and removed exactly. Neither provenance proves contact of the original CAD surfaces or of a separately supplied flattened world-coordinate B-Rep.

docs.title: place_planar_contact_set(local, *, rotation, origin, length_scale=1.0)
docs.text:
Attach an explicit similarity to an already prepared local contact set.

Host validation requires x64, finite origin, a proper orthogonal rotation within 64 binary64 epsilons, and a positive scale whose square is a finite normal binary64 value. The matrix is validated without projection or repair. No geometry, pair relation, or source diagnostic is recomputed. Input arrays are copied; later host mutation does not change the model.

A gap or overlap in the supplied local geometry remains that relation. Supplying the old construction frame beside a flattened B-Rep does not undo its rounded vertex coordinates: prepare the preserved local cells.

docs.title: placed_planar_contact_set_volume_direction(model, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, pivot)
docs.text:
Return one-sided volume rate for a world-coordinate instantaneous motion.

Linear velocity and pivot use world length units; angular velocity uses radians per dimensionless time. The result is world volume per time. JIT and vmap over supplied directions are supported. Like the local evaluator, this nonlinear response is not an ordinary Boolean-volume JVP.

The pullback is s**3 D(R.T v/s, R.T omega, R.T(p-origin)/s). Positive homogeneity gives the equivalent area-scaled evaluation below, avoiding unnecessary overflow in the cubic multiplier or linear-velocity division. Remaining intermediate overflow and unresolvable world-coordinate differences are not repaired. Keep the pivot near the geometry; a distant origin cannot restore information already rounded out of the supplied pivot.

Compensating a changed pivot preserves this instantaneous response. It does not assert equivalence of finite paths using linearly translated rotations. Zero response does not certify a collision-free finite move.

docs.title: prepare_placed_planar_contact_set_reference(fixed_local_cells, moving_local_cells, *, rotation, origin, length_scale=1.0, mode)
docs.text:
Prepare preserved local CAD cells and retain their explicit shared frame.

Local cells follow prepare_planar_contact_set_reference unchanged: same-body or initial cross-body overlap is rejected; positive gaps and lower-dimensional contacts remain in the inventory. The caller supplies the local geometry and the frame; this function does not infer either from transformed world geometry. Every finite edit still needs CAD validation.

Example, with existing local stock/cutter cells and a supplied rotation::

prepared = prepare_placed_planar_contact_set_reference(
    stock_cells, cutter_cells, rotation=rotation, origin=(2, -1, 3),
    length_scale=0.001, mode="zero_residual",
)
rate = placed_planar_contact_set_volume_direction(
    prepared.model, world_velocity, world_angular_velocity, world_pivot,
)
# Pair/source diagnostics remain in prepared.local_reference's units.

docs.title: prepare_located_planar_contact_set_reference(fixed_cells, moving_cells, *, mode)
docs.text:
Use a genuinely shared top-level proper-rigid OCCT Location as provenance.

Every supplied cell must have the same Location datum chain, as compared by OCCT IsEqual. Independently created equal matrices are insufficient. Reflections and nonunit scales beyond frame roundoff are rejected; use explicit local cells and numeric unit metadata for scaled models. At least one non-null cell is required to supply the frame.

Removing this top-level Location leaves the local TShape, orientation and nested geometry unchanged. No inverse transform is baked into vertices. The frame is read from the retained Location, never from a guessed placement or a geometry fit. This is not a general assembly-frame recovery procedure.

An identity Location is allowed and does not recover lost provenance: a flattened input is classified using its existing coordinates and may reject exactly as before. Failures retain the local preparation's pair evidence. The returned model does not certify original source-CAD contact.

docs.title: Finite polyhedral translation
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.polyhedral_translation prepares the complete finite overlap-volume profile along a prescribed translation. Inputs are convex-cell vertex arrays, not CAD solids. Each body's cell interiors must be disjoint, and the bodies must have no initial interior overlap. Preparation computes rational event times and cubic coefficients from the represented geometry; the JAX evaluator uses floating coefficients. It does not fit CAD samples.

from itertools import product

import jax
import numpy as np

from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_translation import (
    polyhedral_translation_slope,
    polyhedral_translation_volume,
    prepare_polyhedral_translation,
)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
box = np.array(list(product((0.0, 1.0), repeat=3)))
path = prepare_polyhedral_translation(
    [box], [box + (1, 1, 0)], (-1, -1, 0), max_step=2.0,
)
value = jax.jit(polyhedral_translation_volume)(path.profile, 0.25)  # 0.0625
left = polyhedral_translation_slope(path.profile, 1.0, side="left")  # 2
right = polyhedral_translation_slope(path.profile, 1.0, side="right")  # -2

This edge-contact example has zero initial slope, grows quadratically, and then loses overlap after the event at step one. Values have cubic length units; step is dimensionless. jit, vmap over steps and ordinary step AD inside open event intervals are supported. At events use explicit one-sided slopes; geometry and direction differentiation are outside the contract.

The profile's floating thresholds round rational event times upward for binary64 query classification. A threshold need not equal the exact event: path.events retains its rational time and exact left/right slope limits. Distinct events without a resolvable floating interval and overflowing or underflowing coefficients are rejected. Out-of-range queries, and slope requests from a side outside the prepared interval, return NaN. Preparation is intended for small convex cells and can be expensive. It does not support rotation or certify that a separate CAD model matches the represented hulls.

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.translation \
  --output /tmp/translation.json --step-output /tmp/translation-edit.step

The benchmark compares independent interval/section references and actual CAD, checks event slopes, and executes a target-volume Cut on a known monotone translation interval. A separate rotating-prism control shows why the initial velocity field cannot determine higher-order finite terms. See the derivation and path limits.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.polyhedral_translation
docs.text:
Finite translation-volume profiles for explicit convex-cell bodies.

Host preparation uses exact rational geometry of represented binary64 vertices. The numerical profile supports JAX step queries. This is neither an importer nor a general Boolean JVP: cells and velocity remain fixed after preparation.

docs.title: PolyhedralTranslationProfile
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Static piece arrays for a fixed pure-translation path.

Create with :func:prepare_polyhedral_translation outside tracing. thresholds round exact event times upward for correct binary64 query classification; they are not generally the actual event times. The mask identifies exactly representable knots. Coefficients use the represented origins and widths, not the unrounded rational event coordinates.

Only the scalar step is an intended differentiation variable. Ordinary AD is supported inside open event chambers, not at a derivative jump. Use the explicit slope query or host event limits at chamber boundaries.

docs.text:

This certifies only the supplied vertex-hull model. It does not establish correspondence to separately supplied CAD or identify every knot as a physical contact event: redundant combinatorial knots can remain.

docs.title: prepare_polyhedral_translation(fixed_cells, moving_cells, velocity, *, max_step)
docs.text:
Prepare exact finite overlap along moving + step * velocity.

Each nonempty body is a list of bounded convex cells, each supplied as finite float64 vertices of shape (N, 3). Every hull must have positive volume; same-body interiors and initial cross-body interiors must be disjoint. Face, edge, point contact and positive gaps are retained. max_step is finite and positive. Step is dimensionless; vertices and velocity share a length unit, and output has its cube as the volume unit.

Preparation enumerates exact hull facets and triple-plane intersections; it is intended for small cells, not large meshes. No volume measurements are fitted. No new contacts are omitted within the prepared interval. Rational event times and one-sided limits remain in the host record. Numerically unresolvable intervals or overflowing/underflowing coefficients raise ValueError instead of merging events or snapping geometry.

Exact global rigid coordinate changes preserve volume; scaling geometry and velocity by s scales volume and step derivatives by s**3. Independently rounding transformed vertices can change the represented contact state and cause preparation to reject; this law does not certify such rounded inputs or CAD import tolerances. Host preparation does not support shape/velocity AD.

Example::

from itertools import product
import jax
import numpy as np

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
box = np.array(list(product((0., 1.), repeat=3)))
prepared = prepare_polyhedral_translation(
    [box], [box + (1., 1., 0.)], (-1., -1., 0.), max_step=2.
)
# Edge contact has zero initial slope but positive finite overlap.
volume = polyhedral_translation_volume(prepared.profile, 0.25)  # 0.0625

docs.title: polyhedral_translation_volume(profile, step)
docs.text:
Evaluate finite overlap, returning NaN outside the prepared interval.

Supports jit/vmap and ordinary step differentiation inside open chambers. The value is continuous at events; its derivative need not be. This evaluates the fixed represented model, not a rebuilt CAD solid.

docs.title: polyhedral_translation_slope(profile, step, *, side='right')
docs.text:
Return the specified one-sided volume/step derivative.

side is static under jit. At a nonrepresentable rational event, a rounded-up threshold lies strictly after it: both sides there use the following chamber. Exact event limits are in the host events record. Missing interval sides (left at zero, right at max_step), nonfinite steps and out-of-range steps return NaN. Derivatives of this slope are not part of the contract.

docs.title: Selecting finite edits with a CAD budget
docs.text:
uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.selection \
  --output /tmp/finite-selection.json

This benchmark compares analytical candidate ordering and CAD confirmation with CAD-only adaptive selection. Its separate amount-refinement panel uses bounded proposals and only returns observed actions. It promises neither monotonic volume along arbitrary motion nor target reachability. A negative error difference relative to the fixed candidate grid is possible when a refined amount improves on every grid action.

Fresh synthetic geometry groups and five grouped train/test partitions keep calibration apart from each evaluated shape; repeated targets are not independent shapes. Reports retain failed or unsupported inputs and targets exceeding a known total-material bound. Probe attempts and final independent Common/Cut checks have separate costs. Cached replay timings do not establish end-to-end speed superiority. The experimental comparison is not a general optimizer API or evidence for arbitrary STEP inputs.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.applications.mold_direction
docs.text:
Mold pull-direction optimization via differentiable undercut analysis.

Given a shape defined by its SDF, estimates the volume of material that would prevent mold removal in a given pull direction. The undercut criterion is SDF-based: a surface point is undercut when its outward normal opposes the pull direction (dot(normal, direction) < 0).

Both the undercut volume and the optimization loop are fully differentiable, enabling gradient-based search over the unit sphere S^2.

docs.title: undercut_volume(shape_sdf, direction, *, lo, hi, resolution=64)
docs.text:
Estimate undercut volume for a mold pull direction.

Undercut is defined as the set of interior points whose SDF spatial gradient (outward normal) opposes the pull direction. Both the interior membership and the undercut condition are smoothed with sigmoid indicators scaled by the grid cell width, ensuring the estimate improves with resolution.

Normals are estimated via central finite differences to avoid NaN gradients at degenerate SDF points (cylinder axis, box center, etc.).

docs.title: brepax.experimental.applications.cad_frame.CadFrame dataclass
docs.text:
Fixed host metadata with x_external = origin + length_scale * x_work.

length_scale is external length units per working length unit. Choose it once from a reference design size, before constructing CAD, and keep it fixed throughout editing. For a 40 mm reference expressed in metres, use length_scale=0.001 to work at size 40. origin is in external units. Directions/rotations are unchanged by this positive uniform scale; any rigid rotation belongs to the supplied geometry model.

Array conversions support JIT, vmap and differentiation when this frame is captured as fixed metadata. A degree-k scalar scales by sk and its gradient with respect to external lengths by s(k-1). The frame itself is not a differentiable model. Prefer x64 for CAD accuracy.

Normalize design dimensions and dimensional meshing/smoothing tolerances BEFORE OCCT construction. This does not infer STEP units, repair existing B-Reps, or guarantee CAD accuracy at arbitrary scales. Output transforms retain OCCT's tolerance semantics; they do not tighten tolerances.

Example

import jax import jax.numpy as jnp frame = CadFrame(0.001, (1.0, 2.0, 3.0)) def sphere_volume(radius): ... r = frame.working_lengths(radius) ... return frame.external_measure(4 * jnp.pi * r**3 / 3, 3) derivative = jax.jit(jax.grad(sphere_volume))(jnp.array(0.003))

docs.title: Qualitative competitor landscape
docs.text:
Important caveat. This is a qualitative feature-coverage table, not a head-to-head numerical benchmark. Numerical comparison would require running the same problem (e.g. volume of a Linkrods-class trimmed-BSpline shape with derivatives w.r.t. control points) through each system, which none of the listed competitors are directly designed to express. The table reports what each system is built to do, not who is faster on a shared benchmark. Cells marked "hypothesis" are best-effort observations from public documentation; treat them as starting points, not citations.

System / Path STEP / B-Rep input Per-face awareness Trimmed BSpline Differentiable volume Per-face metrics Notes BRepAX divergence_volume yes (via OCCT) derived from face triangulation via OCCT BRepMesh yes — through triangle vertex positions yes (this PR's coverage table) strongest production path on this report BRepAX evaluate_stump_volume yes (via OCCT + reconstruction) primitive-based weak (ADR-0020: BSpline patches are not a CSG-Stump DNF half-space ingredient) yes — through primitive parameters not directly analytical-dominant fixtures BRepAX TrimmedCSGStump.volume yes per-face trim metadata stored metadata stored, not on DNF SDF path (ADR-0019, ADR-0020) yes — through primitive parameters not directly bit-equivalent to evaluate_stump_volume on the DNF path Manifold (manifold3d) indirect (mesh only) mesh-level no (mesh) no (Boolean is exact, not differentiable) no hypothesis: robust mesh boolean, not a CAD-differentiable kernel PyTorch3D mesh ops no (mesh only) mesh-level no (mesh) partial (mesh deformations are differentiable) no hypothesis: differentiable mesh operations, not B-Rep JAX-FEM no (FE mesh) element-level no (mesh) yes — but for FE objectives, not CAD volume no hypothesis: physics solver, not a CAD geometry kernel

The framing BRepAX is built around — gradients flow from STEP / B-Rep through to a JAX scalar — does not have an obvious head-to-head counterpart in the listed systems, because they enter the pipeline at a different stage (mesh, or FE mesh). This is the BRepAX position to test, not assume; the right way to falsify it is to run a published benchmark that asks each system to solve the same B-Rep-rooted optimisation problem. No such benchmark is bundled with this PR.

What is not claimed by this report:

  • No "first" or "unique" claim about any BRepAX path. Other research projects exist on differentiable B-Rep, signed distance functions on trimmed surfaces, and topology-aware boolean differentiation; this report does not survey them.
  • No quantitative speed comparison against any external system.
  • No claim that BRepAX outperforms any competitor on tasks they were designed for. Manifold's exact mesh boolean and JAX-FEM's PDE solver are not in scope here.

What this report does assert:

  • The numbers in volume accuracy and face-level metric coverage are reproducible from the bundled command on the bundled fixtures.
  • The CSG-Stump and TrimmedCSGStump rows being equal is consistent with the negative-result ADRs (ADR-0019, ADR-0020).
  • Per-face metric NaN counts on cone / torus / BSpline faces in mean_curvature_per_face are the documented analytical-handler deferral, not failures.

class BSplineSurface(Primitive):
    """B-spline surface defined by a control point grid and knot vectors.

    The SDF is computed via closest-point projection onto the surface.
    Control points are differentiable design variables: ``jax.grad``
    flows through the unrolled Newton projection.

    Attributes:
        control_points: Control point grid, shape ``(n_u, n_v, 3)``.
        knots_u: Knot vector in u-direction.
        knots_v: Knot vector in v-direction.
        degree_u: Polynomial degree in u.
        degree_v: Polynomial degree in v.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> pts = jnp.array([[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],
        ...                  [[0,1,0],[1,1,0]]], dtype=float)
        >>> knots = jnp.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
        >>> surf = BSplineSurface(
        ...     control_points=pts, knots_u=knots, knots_v=knots,
        ...     degree_u=1, degree_v=1,
        ... )
        >>> d = surf.sdf(jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]))
    """

    control_points: Float[Array, "nu nv 3"]
    knots_u: Array = eqx.field()
    knots_v: Array = eqx.field()
    degree_u: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    degree_v: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    weights: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    sign_flip: float = eqx.field(default=1.0, static=True)
    param_u_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    param_v_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    coarse_positions: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    coarse_normals: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_polygon: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_mask: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the B-spline surface.

        For batched inputs, each point is projected independently via
        Newton iteration.
        """
        shape = x.shape[:-1]
        flat = x.reshape(-1, 3)

        # Coarse grid sampling: compute once, reuse for all query points
        from brepax.nurbs.projection import _COARSE_GRID

        u_lo = self.knots_u[self.degree_u]
        u_hi = self.knots_u[-self.degree_u - 1]
        v_lo = self.knots_v[self.degree_v]
        v_hi = self.knots_v[-self.degree_v - 1]
        us = jnp.linspace(u_lo, u_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        vs = jnp.linspace(v_lo, v_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        u_grid, v_grid = jnp.meshgrid(us, vs, indexing="ij")
        u_flat_g = u_grid.ravel()
        v_flat_g = v_grid.ravel()

        def _eval_sample(u: Array, v: Array) -> Array:
            return evaluate_surface(
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u,
                v,
                self.weights,
            )

        samples = jax.vmap(_eval_sample)(u_flat_g, v_flat_g)

        def _single_sdf(q: Array) -> Array:
            # Find closest coarse sample (stop_gradient: argmin is non-diff)
            dists = jnp.sum((samples - q) ** 2, axis=-1)
            best = jnp.argmin(dists)
            u0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(u_flat_g[best])
            v0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(v_flat_g[best])
            return bspline_sdf(
                q,
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u0=u0,
                v0=v0,
                weights=self.weights,
                param_u_range=self.param_u_range,
                param_v_range=self.param_v_range,
                sign_flip=self.sign_flip,
                coarse_positions=self.coarse_positions,
                coarse_normals=self.coarse_normals,
            )

        result = jax.vmap(_single_sdf)(flat)
        return result.reshape(shape)

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        params: dict[str, Array] = {
            "control_points": self.control_points,
            "knots_u": self.knots_u,
            "knots_v": self.knots_v,
        }
        if self.weights is not None:
            params["weights"] = self.weights
        return params

class Box(Primitive):
    """An axis-aligned box defined by center and half-extents.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the box (3,).
        half_extents: Half-size in each dimension (3,).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    half_extents: Float[Array, "3"]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the box surface."""
        q = jnp.abs(x - self.center) - self.half_extents
        qp = jnp.maximum(q, 0.0)
        # eps avoids NaN gradient from norm at zero (same pattern as FiniteCylinder)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(qp**2, axis=-1) + 1e-20)
        is_outside = jnp.max(q, axis=-1) > 0
        outside = jnp.where(is_outside, outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.max(q, axis=-1), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"center": self.center, "half_extents": self.half_extents}

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Box volume: 8 * hx * hy * hz."""
        return 8.0 * jnp.prod(self.half_extents)

class Cone(Primitive):
    """An infinite cone defined by apex position, axis direction, and half-angle.

    The cone extends infinitely from the apex along the axis direction.
    The SDF is positive outside, negative inside.

    Attributes:
        apex: Apex point of the cone (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector from apex (3,). Must be normalized.
        angle: Half-angle in radians (0, pi/2).
    """

    apex: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    angle: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cone surface."""
        v = x - self.apex
        # Distance along axis
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2, 1e-20))
        sin_a = jnp.sin(self.angle)
        cos_a = jnp.cos(self.angle)
        # Signed distance: positive outside cone, negative inside
        return jnp.where(
            h >= 0,
            perp * cos_a - h * sin_a,
            jnp.sqrt(perp**2 + h**2),
        )

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"apex": self.apex, "axis": self.axis, "angle": self.angle}

class Cylinder(Primitive):
    """An infinite cylinder defined by a point on the axis, axis direction, and radius.

    The SDF measures perpendicular distance from the axis line minus the radius.
    The cylinder extends infinitely along the axis direction.

    Attributes:
        point: A point on the cylinder axis (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Scalar radius (must be positive).
    """

    point: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cylinder surface.

        Computes the perpendicular distance from each query point to
        the cylinder axis, then subtracts the radius.
        """
        # Vector from axis point to query
        v = x - self.point
        # Project onto axis to get parallel component
        proj_len = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        # Perpendicular component
        perp = v - proj_len * self.axis
        perp_dist = jnp.linalg.norm(perp, axis=-1)
        return perp_dist - self.radius  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"point": self.point, "axis": self.axis, "radius": self.radius}

class FiniteCylinder(Primitive):
    """A finite cylinder (capped) defined by center, axis, radius, and height.

    The cylinder is centered at `center` and extends `height/2` in each
    direction along `axis`.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the cylinder (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Cylinder radius (must be positive).
        height: Total height along the axis (must be positive).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]
    height: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the finite cylinder surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Axial distance from center
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(perp_sq, 1e-20))

        # Signed distances to the two constraints
        d_radial = perp - self.radius
        d_axial = jnp.abs(h) - self.height / 2.0

        # SDF of intersection of infinite cylinder and slab.
        # Use sqrt with eps to avoid NaN gradient at [0, 0].
        dr = jnp.maximum(d_radial, 0.0)
        da = jnp.maximum(d_axial, 0.0)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(dr**2 + da**2 + 1e-20)
        # Subtract the eps contribution when truly outside
        outside = jnp.where((dr > 0) | (da > 0), outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.maximum(d_radial, d_axial), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "axis": self.axis,
            "radius": self.radius,
            "height": self.height,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Finite cylinder volume: pi * r^2 * h."""
        return jnp.pi * self.radius**2 * self.height

def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
    """Signed distance from query points to the finite cylinder surface."""
    v = x - self.center
    # Axial distance from center
    h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
    # Perpendicular distance from axis
    perp_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
    perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(perp_sq, 1e-20))

    # Signed distances to the two constraints
    d_radial = perp - self.radius
    d_axial = jnp.abs(h) - self.height / 2.0

    # SDF of intersection of infinite cylinder and slab.
    # Use sqrt with eps to avoid NaN gradient at [0, 0].
    dr = jnp.maximum(d_radial, 0.0)
    da = jnp.maximum(d_axial, 0.0)
    outside = jnp.sqrt(dr**2 + da**2 + 1e-20)
    # Subtract the eps contribution when truly outside
    outside = jnp.where((dr > 0) | (da > 0), outside, 0.0)
    inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.maximum(d_radial, d_axial), 0.0)
    return outside + inside

class Primitive(eqx.Module):
    """Base class for all geometric primitives.

    Each primitive exposes an SDF, gradient w.r.t. spatial coordinates,
    and a list of design parameters that gradients can flow into.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... dim"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Evaluate the signed distance function at query points."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Analytical volume of this primitive.

        Returns the finite volume for bounded primitives (Sphere, Box, etc.).
        Unbounded primitives (Cylinder, Plane, Cone) return inf.
        Override in subclasses with known analytical formulas.
        Differentiable via jax.grad for gradient computation.
        """
        # Default: unbounded primitive has infinite volume
        import jax.numpy as jnp

        return jnp.array(jnp.inf)

class Torus(Primitive):
    """A torus defined by center, axis, major radius, and minor radius.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the torus (3,).
        axis: Unit normal to the torus plane (3,). Must be normalized.
        major_radius: Distance from center to tube center.
        minor_radius: Tube radius.
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    major_radius: Float[Array, ""]
    minor_radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the torus surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Component along axis (height above torus plane)
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Component in the torus plane (distance from center axis)
        v_plane_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        v_plane = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(v_plane_sq, 1e-20))
        # Distance from the tube center ring
        q = jnp.sqrt((v_plane - self.major_radius) ** 2 + h**2)
        return q - self.minor_radius

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "major_radius": self.major_radius,
            "minor_radius": self.minor_radius,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Torus volume: 2 * pi^2 * R * r^2."""
        return 2.0 * jnp.pi**2 * self.major_radius * self.minor_radius**2

class Box(Primitive):
    """An axis-aligned box defined by center and half-extents.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the box (3,).
        half_extents: Half-size in each dimension (3,).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    half_extents: Float[Array, "3"]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the box surface."""
        q = jnp.abs(x - self.center) - self.half_extents
        qp = jnp.maximum(q, 0.0)
        # eps avoids NaN gradient from norm at zero (same pattern as FiniteCylinder)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(qp**2, axis=-1) + 1e-20)
        is_outside = jnp.max(q, axis=-1) > 0
        outside = jnp.where(is_outside, outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.max(q, axis=-1), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"center": self.center, "half_extents": self.half_extents}

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Box volume: 8 * hx * hy * hz."""
        return 8.0 * jnp.prod(self.half_extents)

class BSplineSurface(Primitive):
    """B-spline surface defined by a control point grid and knot vectors.

    The SDF is computed via closest-point projection onto the surface.
    Control points are differentiable design variables: ``jax.grad``
    flows through the unrolled Newton projection.

    Attributes:
        control_points: Control point grid, shape ``(n_u, n_v, 3)``.
        knots_u: Knot vector in u-direction.
        knots_v: Knot vector in v-direction.
        degree_u: Polynomial degree in u.
        degree_v: Polynomial degree in v.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> pts = jnp.array([[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],
        ...                  [[0,1,0],[1,1,0]]], dtype=float)
        >>> knots = jnp.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
        >>> surf = BSplineSurface(
        ...     control_points=pts, knots_u=knots, knots_v=knots,
        ...     degree_u=1, degree_v=1,
        ... )
        >>> d = surf.sdf(jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]))
    """

    control_points: Float[Array, "nu nv 3"]
    knots_u: Array = eqx.field()
    knots_v: Array = eqx.field()
    degree_u: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    degree_v: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    weights: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    sign_flip: float = eqx.field(default=1.0, static=True)
    param_u_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    param_v_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    coarse_positions: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    coarse_normals: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_polygon: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_mask: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the B-spline surface.

        For batched inputs, each point is projected independently via
        Newton iteration.
        """
        shape = x.shape[:-1]
        flat = x.reshape(-1, 3)

        # Coarse grid sampling: compute once, reuse for all query points
        from brepax.nurbs.projection import _COARSE_GRID

        u_lo = self.knots_u[self.degree_u]
        u_hi = self.knots_u[-self.degree_u - 1]
        v_lo = self.knots_v[self.degree_v]
        v_hi = self.knots_v[-self.degree_v - 1]
        us = jnp.linspace(u_lo, u_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        vs = jnp.linspace(v_lo, v_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        u_grid, v_grid = jnp.meshgrid(us, vs, indexing="ij")
        u_flat_g = u_grid.ravel()
        v_flat_g = v_grid.ravel()

        def _eval_sample(u: Array, v: Array) -> Array:
            return evaluate_surface(
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u,
                v,
                self.weights,
            )

        samples = jax.vmap(_eval_sample)(u_flat_g, v_flat_g)

        def _single_sdf(q: Array) -> Array:
            # Find closest coarse sample (stop_gradient: argmin is non-diff)
            dists = jnp.sum((samples - q) ** 2, axis=-1)
            best = jnp.argmin(dists)
            u0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(u_flat_g[best])
            v0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(v_flat_g[best])
            return bspline_sdf(
                q,
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u0=u0,
                v0=v0,
                weights=self.weights,
                param_u_range=self.param_u_range,
                param_v_range=self.param_v_range,
                sign_flip=self.sign_flip,
                coarse_positions=self.coarse_positions,
                coarse_normals=self.coarse_normals,
            )

        result = jax.vmap(_single_sdf)(flat)
        return result.reshape(shape)

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        params: dict[str, Array] = {
            "control_points": self.control_points,
            "knots_u": self.knots_u,
            "knots_v": self.knots_v,
        }
        if self.weights is not None:
            params["weights"] = self.weights
        return params

class Cone(Primitive):
    """An infinite cone defined by apex position, axis direction, and half-angle.

    The cone extends infinitely from the apex along the axis direction.
    The SDF is positive outside, negative inside.

    Attributes:
        apex: Apex point of the cone (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector from apex (3,). Must be normalized.
        angle: Half-angle in radians (0, pi/2).
    """

    apex: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    angle: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cone surface."""
        v = x - self.apex
        # Distance along axis
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2, 1e-20))
        sin_a = jnp.sin(self.angle)
        cos_a = jnp.cos(self.angle)
        # Signed distance: positive outside cone, negative inside
        return jnp.where(
            h >= 0,
            perp * cos_a - h * sin_a,
            jnp.sqrt(perp**2 + h**2),
        )

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"apex": self.apex, "axis": self.axis, "angle": self.angle}

class Cylinder(Primitive):
    """An infinite cylinder defined by a point on the axis, axis direction, and radius.

    The SDF measures perpendicular distance from the axis line minus the radius.
    The cylinder extends infinitely along the axis direction.

    Attributes:
        point: A point on the cylinder axis (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Scalar radius (must be positive).
    """

    point: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cylinder surface.

        Computes the perpendicular distance from each query point to
        the cylinder axis, then subtracts the radius.
        """
        # Vector from axis point to query
        v = x - self.point
        # Project onto axis to get parallel component
        proj_len = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        # Perpendicular component
        perp = v - proj_len * self.axis
        perp_dist = jnp.linalg.norm(perp, axis=-1)
        return perp_dist - self.radius  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"point": self.point, "axis": self.axis, "radius": self.radius}

class FiniteCylinder(Primitive):
    """A finite cylinder (capped) defined by center, axis, radius, and height.

    The cylinder is centered at `center` and extends `height/2` in each
    direction along `axis`.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the cylinder (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Cylinder radius (must be positive).
        height: Total height along the axis (must be positive).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]
    height: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the finite cylinder surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Axial distance from center
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(perp_sq, 1e-20))

        # Signed distances to the two constraints
        d_radial = perp - self.radius
        d_axial = jnp.abs(h) - self.height / 2.0

        # SDF of intersection of infinite cylinder and slab.
        # Use sqrt with eps to avoid NaN gradient at [0, 0].
        dr = jnp.maximum(d_radial, 0.0)
        da = jnp.maximum(d_axial, 0.0)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(dr**2 + da**2 + 1e-20)
        # Subtract the eps contribution when truly outside
        outside = jnp.where((dr > 0) | (da > 0), outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.maximum(d_radial, d_axial), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "axis": self.axis,
            "radius": self.radius,
            "height": self.height,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Finite cylinder volume: pi * r^2 * h."""
        return jnp.pi * self.radius**2 * self.height

docs.title: foot
docs.text:
Analytical foot-of-perpendicular on primitive surfaces.

Each function returns the closest point on an infinite analytical surface (plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) to a query point. Closed form given the primitive parameters; fully differentiable w.r.t. both the query and the primitive parameters.

Scope is the untrimmed surface only; trim-boundary interaction is layered on via Marschner composition in a separate module. Cone and torus inner-region degeneracies (apex, tube axis) are handled with an epsilon guard on the radial direction.

Zero-denominator handling uses a safe-square-then-sqrt pattern that keeps both forward and gradient finite at the degenerate boundary. jnp.linalg.norm(v) has infinite derivative at v = 0; since jnp.where evaluates both branches in the VJP, a naive guard on norm still leaks NaN into jax.grad. The pattern used here switches on the squared norm before sqrt, so the sqrt argument is bounded below by 1 when the query is degenerate:

sq = sum(v * v)
is_ok = sq > eps_sq
safe_sq = where(is_ok, sq, 1.0)
norm = sqrt(safe_sq)   # always >= 1 at the degenerate point
direction = where(is_ok, v / norm, fallback)

docs.title: foot_on_cone(query, apex, axis, angle)
docs.text:
Closest point on the half-cone extending forward of apex.

The cone is the surface r(h) = h * tan(angle) for h >= 0 along axis. For queries that project to h < 0 the foot is clamped to apex.

Source code in src/brepax/primitives/foot.py 
def foot_on_cone(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    apex: Float[Array, 3],
    axis: Float[Array, 3],
    angle: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on the half-cone extending forward of ``apex``.

    The cone is the surface ``r(h) = h * tan(angle)`` for ``h >= 0``
    along ``axis``.  For queries that project to ``h < 0`` the foot is
    clamped to ``apex``.
    """
    v = query - apex
    h = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - h * axis
    radial_norm, radial_dir = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    cos_a = jnp.cos(angle)
    sin_a = jnp.sin(angle)
    t = h * cos_a + radial_norm * sin_a
    t = jnp.maximum(t, 0.0)
    return apex + t * (cos_a * axis + sin_a * radial_dir)

def foot_on_cylinder(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    point: Float[Array, 3],
    axis: Float[Array, 3],
    radius: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on an infinite cylinder of ``radius`` about the axis.

    On the axis itself the radial direction is ill-defined; a canonical
    unit vector orthogonal to ``axis`` is used to keep the computation
    differentiable.
    """
    v = query - point
    axial_len = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - axial_len * axis
    _, direction = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    return point + axial_len * axis + radius * direction

Closest point on the torus tube around the major ring.

Project to the tube-center ring first, then shift outward by minor_radius. On the central axis (radial == 0) a canonical in-plane direction is used; on the tube center itself (dq == 0) the fallback is the radial direction.

def foot_on_torus(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    center: Float[Array, 3],
    axis: Float[Array, 3],
    major_radius: Float[Array, ""],
    minor_radius: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on the torus tube around the major ring.

    Project to the tube-center ring first, then shift outward by
    ``minor_radius``.  On the central axis (``radial == 0``) a canonical
    in-plane direction is used; on the tube center itself
    (``dq == 0``) the fallback is the radial direction.
    """
    v = query - center
    h = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - h * axis
    _, radial_dir = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    tube_center = center + major_radius * radial_dir
    dq = query - tube_center
    _, dq_dir = _safe_unit(dq, radial_dir)
    return tube_center + minor_radius * dq_dir

class Torus(Primitive):
    """A torus defined by center, axis, major radius, and minor radius.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the torus (3,).
        axis: Unit normal to the torus plane (3,). Must be normalized.
        major_radius: Distance from center to tube center.
        minor_radius: Tube radius.
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    major_radius: Float[Array, ""]
    minor_radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the torus surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Component along axis (height above torus plane)
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Component in the torus plane (distance from center axis)
        v_plane_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        v_plane = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(v_plane_sq, 1e-20))
        # Distance from the tube center ring
        q = jnp.sqrt((v_plane - self.major_radius) ** 2 + h**2)
        return q - self.minor_radius

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "major_radius": self.major_radius,
            "minor_radius": self.minor_radius,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Torus volume: 2 * pi^2 * R * r^2."""
        return 2.0 * jnp.pi**2 * self.major_radius * self.minor_radius**2
